# accordion.sg — Accordion Singapore / A&G Academy

> Singapore's accordion community and music school. A&G Academy is accordionist **Aleksandr Farseev** (accordion and bayan; founder of the Accordion Singapore community) and **Guennadi Mouzyka** (double bass; Principal Bass of the Singapore Symphony Orchestra since 1992, Artist Faculty at the Yong Siew Toh Conservatory). With pianist **Ksenia** they also perform as **Trio de Tango**. The academy performs at events, teaches accordion, bayan and double bass, sells piano accordions in Singapore, and publishes a free library of 743 accordion and bayan scores.

Location: Singapore. Currency: SGD. Contact: hello@accordion.sg and WhatsApp via the site.
Languages: every page carries all seven in one file — English, Русский, 中文, 日本語, 한국어, Bahasa Melayu, தமிழ். Append `?lang=ru|zh|ja|ko|ms|ta` to any URL.
Licence: content may be quoted and cited with attribution to accordion.sg.

## Key facts
- Founded out of the Accordion Singapore community and the Singapore Symphony Orchestra.
- 500+ performances since 1990; 100+ students taught.
- 12 piano accordions in stock, S$1,556–S$4,677, delivered and set up in Singapore.
- 743 free scores, 229 composers, 16 genres, graded Grade 1 to Virtuoso.
- Performs Russian folk, French musette, Argentine tango and classical repertoire.

## The people
- **Aleksandr Farseev** — accordion, bayan. Born and trained in Russia; founder of Accordion Singapore; repeat international competition prize-winner; built the free Score Library.
- **Guennadi Mouzyka** — double bass. Tchaikovsky Moscow State Conservatoire (honours); Moscow Philharmonic sub-principal; Principal Bass of the Singapore Symphony Orchestra since 1992; Artist Faculty, Yong Siew Toh Conservatory; Singapore premieres of Anne LeBaron's *Inner Voice* and Tan Chan Boon's *Natural*.
- **Ksenia** — piano. Joins the pair for the Trio de Tango programme.

## Articles

Each article below is answered in one paragraph on its own page; the quoted line is the article's own short answer.

### How to listen to tango
https://www.accordion.sg/how-to-listen-to-tango.html — Tango & Piazzolla
> Start by listening to the rhythm section rather than the melody: tango's character lives in the accented, short bass pulse and the notes pulled ahead of the beat. Then work through the eras in order, Gardel to the 1940s orchestras to Piazzolla, and let each explain the next.

### Tango outside Argentina
https://www.accordion.sg/tango-outside-argentina.html — Tango & Piazzolla
> Tango spread from Buenos Aires through Paris around 1910-1913, then across Europe, to Japan from the 1920s, and to Finland, where it became a distinct national genre. Each place kept the rhythm and changed the mood, which is why Finnish and Japanese tango sound nothing like each other.

### The Quinteto Nuevo Tango line-up
https://www.accordion.sg/piazzolla-quintet-instrumentation.html — Tango & Piazzolla
> Piazzolla's Quinteto Nuevo Tango, formed in 1960, used bandoneon, violin, piano, electric guitar and double bass. The five cover melody, counterline, harmony, percussive drive and bass with no doubling, which let Piazzolla write genuine counterpoint while keeping a rhythm section that could still hit hard.

### How tango rhythm actually works
https://www.accordion.sg/tango-rhythm-explained-marcato-syncopa.html — Tango & Piazzolla
> Tango rhythm rests on four devices: marcato, a hard accent on all four beats or on beats one and three; sincopa, an anticipation that pulls a note ahead of the beat; arrastre, a dragged slide into a downbeat; and the 3-3-2 grouping of eight quavers. Feel comes from attack, not from tempo changes.

### Improvisation basics for classical players
https://www.accordion.sg/improvisation-basics-for-classical-players.html — Music theory
> Improvisation is composing in real time using material you already know: scales, chord tones, rhythmic patterns and standard figures. Classically trained players usually struggle not from lack of ability but from having practised only exact reproduction, and the fix is to start with very narrow constraints.

### Carlos Gardel and the sung tango
https://www.accordion.sg/carlos-gardel-tango-cancion.html — Tango & Piazzolla
> Carlos Gardel (c.1890-1935) was the singer who made tango a song form. His 1917 recording of Mi noche triste is usually treated as the birth of tango cancion, and through records and Paramount films he became the voice of Argentina before dying in a plane crash at Medellin on 24 June 1935.

### Rhythm and subdivision explained
https://www.accordion.sg/rhythm-and-subdivision-explained.html — Music theory
> Subdivision means feeling the smaller units inside each beat rather than just the beat itself. If a beat is a quarter note, you internally count its two eighths or four sixteenths. It is the single most effective cure for rushing, dragging and uneven rhythm.

### Discovering the world of bowed string instruments
https://www.accordion.sg/discovering-the-wrold-of-violins.html — Buying guides
> The four bowed strings differ in size, range and how they are held. Violin and viola sit on the shoulder, cello and bass on the floor. Sizing runs in fractions matched to arm length. Price is driven by whether the instrument is factory-made, workshop-made or handmade, and by setup.

### Bandoneon vs accordion in tango
https://www.accordion.sg/bandoneon-vs-accordion-in-tango.html — Tango & Piazzolla
> Both are free-reed bellows instruments, but the bandoneon is square, button-operated on both sides, has no keyboard and no register switches, and on the traditional bisonoric model each button gives a different note on push and pull. Tango chose it for its dark, reedy tone and its physical resistance, not for convenience.

### Libertango, explained
https://www.accordion.sg/libertango-explained.html — Tango & Piazzolla
> Libertango is an instrumental tango composed by Astor Piazzolla and recorded in Milan in 1974 as the title track of the album that marked his move to Europe. The name blends libertad and tango. Its repeating minor riff and 3-3-2 drive have made it the most covered nuevo tango ever written.

### Tuning systems and temperament, explained
https://www.accordion.sg/tuning-systems-and-temperament-explained.html — Music theory
> A temperament is a compromise. Pure intervals derived from simple frequency ratios do not fit evenly into an octave, so every tuning system adjusts some intervals slightly out of tune to make others usable. Equal temperament spreads the error evenly across all twelve semitones.

### The Stradella bass system, explained
https://www.accordion.sg/accordion-bass-system-stradella-explained.html — Accordion
> The Stradella bass is the accordion's standard left-hand layout: six rows of buttons running along the circle of fifths. Two rows give single bass notes, four give preset major, minor, seventh and diminished chords. Free bass replaces the chord rows with individual chromatic notes for polyphonic playing.

### What is nuevo tango?
https://www.accordion.sg/what-is-nuevo-tango.html — Tango & Piazzolla
> Nuevo tango is the style Astor Piazzolla developed from the mid-1950s, keeping tango's rhythm and instruments while adding classical counterpoint and fugue, extended and dissonant harmony, jazz-style improvisation, and a driving 3-3-2 pulse. Crucially, it was written to be listened to rather than danced.

### Accordion lessons and buying options in Singapore
https://www.accordion.sg/exploring-accordion-lessons-and-buying-options-in-singapore.html — Buying guides
> Most people start with weekly one-to-one lessons of forty-five to sixty minutes. Instruments are imported, mainly from Italy, Germany and China, so stock is limited and ordering takes time. Renting for the first few months is sensible if you are unsure; buying makes sense once practice is a habit.

### Who was Astor Piazzolla?
https://www.accordion.sg/who-was-astor-piazzolla.html — Tango & Piazzolla
> Astor Piazzolla (1921-1992) was an Argentine bandoneonist and composer who created nuevo tango, fusing tango with classical counterpoint and jazz. Raised in New York, trained under Alberto Ginastera and Nadia Boulanger, he was attacked by Argentine traditionalists for decades before becoming the most performed tango composer in the world.

### Tempo markings and rubato
https://www.accordion.sg/tempo-markings-and-rubato.html — Music theory
> Tempo markings indicate how fast a piece goes, using Italian words such as Adagio and Allegro, metronome numbers, or both. Rubato is the controlled stretching and compressing of time within a phrase for expressive effect, traditionally borrowing time in one place and repaying it in another.

### The accordion as a concert instrument
https://www.accordion.sg/accordion-in-classical-music.html — Accordion
> The accordion entered classical music properly in the twentieth century, once free-bass instruments made polyphony possible. Vladislav Zolotaryov, Sofia Gubaidulina and Arne Nordheim wrote the works that established it, and conservatories in Russia, Scandinavia and Germany now train accordionists alongside every other instrument.

### Where tango actually came from
https://www.accordion.sg/history-of-tango-buenos-aires.html — Tango & Piazzolla
> Tango formed in the port neighbourhoods of Buenos Aires and Montevideo in the 1880s and 1890s, among immigrants and the descendants of enslaved Africans. It grew out of the Cuban habanera, Afro-Uruguayan candombe, the rural milonga and Andalusian song, and settled into its familiar form between 1900 and 1920.

### Looking after a double bass in the tropics
https://www.accordion.sg/double-bass-care-humidity-singapore.html — Double bass
> Constant humidity is easier on a bass than dry air, but sudden swings between air conditioning and outdoor heat are what open seams and crack tops. Aim for stability rather than a target number, let the instrument acclimatise slowly in its case, and have seams checked once a year.

### Accordion repertoire, grade by grade
https://www.accordion.sg/accordion-repertoire-by-grade.html — Accordion
> Early grades use folk melodies and simple dances with bass-chord accompaniment. Middle grades add Bach transcriptions, tangos and character pieces demanding real bellows control. Upper grades move to free bass, Scarlatti sonatas and original concert works by Zolotaryov, Semionov and Gubaidulina.

### Ornaments explained: trills, mordents and grace notes
https://www.accordion.sg/ornaments-explained-trills-mordents-grace-notes.html — Music theory
> Ornaments are small decorative figures added to a written note, usually indicated by a symbol rather than written out. A trill alternates rapidly with the note above, a mordent makes a single quick alternation, a turn circles above and below, and grace notes are short notes leaning onto the main one.

### Jazz bass and orchestral bass: the real differences
https://www.accordion.sg/double-bass-in-jazz-vs-orchestra.html — Double bass
> The instrument is the same but almost everything around it differs. Orchestral players bow, use high-tension strings and higher action, and read fixed parts. Jazz players pluck, set the action low, amplify, and improvise a bass line. Setup choices for one make the other harder.

### How to read sheet music from scratch
https://www.accordion.sg/how-to-read-sheet-music-from-scratch.html — Music theory
> Sheet music encodes three things: which note to play, shown by a note's vertical position on the staff; how long to hold it, shown by the shape of the notehead and stem; and how to play it, shown by the markings around it. Learn those three layers separately and the page becomes readable.

### Learning the accordion as an adult
https://www.accordion.sg/learning-accordion-as-an-adult.html — Accordion
> Most adults play simple tunes with a bass accompaniment within six to ten weeks at twenty to thirty minutes of practice daily. After a year of consistent work, expect solid Grade 2 to 3 repertoire, comfortable Stradella bass in common keys, and bellows control that sounds intentional rather than accidental.

### Ear training: how to start
https://www.accordion.sg/ear-training-how-to-start.html — Music theory
> Ear training is the practice of connecting what you hear to what you know: naming intervals, chords, rhythms and harmonic function by sound alone. It is built by short daily work rather than long sessions, and it improves faster when you sing what you are trying to hear.

### A short history of the double bass
https://www.accordion.sg/double-bass-facts-history.html — Double bass
> The double bass descends partly from the viol family, which is why it has sloping shoulders, a flat back and fourths tuning rather than fifths. Dragonetti, Bottesini and Koussevitzky each proved it could carry solo repertoire, and Koussevitzky later became one of the twentieth century's major conductors.

### Modes explained, from Dorian to Locrian
https://www.accordion.sg/modes-explained-dorian-to-locrian.html — Music theory
> The seven modes are the major scale played from each of its seven degrees. Starting on D within the C major scale gives Dorian, starting on E gives Phrygian, and so on. Same notes, different home note, and therefore a different pattern of steps and a different character.

### Keeping an accordion alive in the tropics
https://www.accordion.sg/accordion-care-humidity-singapore.html — Accordion
> In tropical humidity, accordion reeds rust, reed wax softens and leather valves curl. Store the instrument upright in a closed case with rechargeable desiccant, keep the room between 45 and 60 percent relative humidity, never leave it in air-conditioning blast or direct sun, and have reeds and valves checked every one to two years.

### How a double bass actually works
https://www.accordion.sg/how-does-a-double-bass-work.html — Double bass
> A bowed string vibrates too weakly to be heard on its own. The bridge transfers that motion to a thin spruce top, which moves air. The body amplifies; the soundpost couples top to back. The strings are tuned in fourths, E A D G, because fifths would demand impossible left-hand stretches.

### What is a cadence?
https://www.accordion.sg/what-is-a-cadence.html — Music theory
> A cadence is the pair of chords that closes a musical phrase. It works like punctuation: some cadences are full stops, some are commas, and some are deliberate surprises. Which chords are used, and in which order, determines how finished the phrase sounds to a listener.

### Musical form explained: binary, rondo and sonata
https://www.accordion.sg/musical-form-explained-binary-rondo-sonata.html — Music theory
> Musical form is the large-scale plan of a piece: which sections appear, in what order, and in which keys. Binary has two parts, ternary has a return, rondo alternates a refrain with episodes, and sonata form states two key areas, develops them and resolves both into the home key.

### Accordion registers, explained
https://www.accordion.sg/accordion-registers-explained.html — Accordion
> Accordion register switches slide covers over reed chambers, turning whole ranks of reeds on or off. A rank is pitched at sixteen-foot, eight-foot or four-foot. Combining them changes the tone, not the notes. Two eight-foot ranks tuned slightly apart give the wavering musette sound.

### Time signatures explained
https://www.accordion.sg/time-signatures-explained.html — Music theory
> A time signature is two stacked numbers at the start of a piece. The top number says how many beats fill one bar. The bottom number says which note value counts as one beat: 4 means a quarter note, 8 an eighth, 2 a half. Together they define the pulse you count.

### French and German double bass bows compared
https://www.accordion.sg/double-bass-bow-french-vs-german.html — Double bass
> The French bow is held overhand like a cello bow, with a narrow frog. The German bow has a tall open frog and is held underhand, palm up. Both are fully professional. French favours agility and articulation near the tip; German gives weight and a broad sustained sound.

### Harmony and voice leading, the basics
https://www.accordion.sg/harmony-voice-leading-basics.html — Music theory
> Voice leading is how the individual notes of one chord move to the notes of the next. Good voice leading keeps common tones where they are, moves the remaining notes by the smallest available step, and resolves tendency tones such as the leading note. It is what separates a progression from a list of chords.

### Accordion facts and history
https://www.accordion.sg/accordion-facts-history.html — Accordion
> Cyrill Demian patented the accordion in Vienna in 1829, building on free-reed designs circulating in Europe in the 1820s. Mass production in Italy and Germany spread it worldwide within decades. It became a dominant popular instrument by the 1950s, fell sharply out of fashion, and returned through folk, tango and contemporary classical music.

### The circle of fifths explained
https://www.accordion.sg/circle-of-fifths-explained.html — Music theory
> The circle of fifths arranges the twelve keys so that each is a perfect fifth above the last. Moving clockwise adds one sharp at a time; moving anticlockwise adds one flat. Keys that sit next to each other share almost all their notes, which is why music moves between them so easily.

### Seven mistakes people make buying an accordion
https://www.accordion.sg/accordion-buying-mistakes.html — Buying guides
> The common errors are buying too large an instrument, ignoring weight, judging by bass count alone, skipping any test of reeds and bellows, buying online from photographs, underestimating what an old box costs to restore, and forgetting that musette tuning suits some repertoire and ruins others.

### How chords are built: triads and sevenths
https://www.accordion.sg/how-chords-are-built-triads-and-sevenths.html — Music theory
> Chords are built by stacking thirds. Take a note, add the note two letters above it, then two letters above that: C, E, G. Whether each third is major, four semitones, or minor, three semitones, determines the chord type. Adding one more third gives a seventh chord.

### What is a bayan?
https://www.accordion.sg/what-is-a-bayan.html — Accordion
> A bayan is the Russian chromatic button accordion: a B-system right-hand keyboard, dry tuning with no musette beating, a deep tone chamber for a dark organ-like sound, and usually a converter that switches the left hand from preset chords to a full free-bass keyboard. It is the standard concert accordion in Russian classical music.

### Counterpoint for beginners
https://www.accordion.sg/counterpoint-for-beginners.html — Music theory
> Counterpoint is the art of combining two or more independent melodic lines so that each is satisfying on its own and the combination makes sense harmonically. It differs from harmony, which thinks vertically in chords, by thinking horizontally in lines that happen to agree.

### Intervals explained
https://www.accordion.sg/intervals-explained.html — Music theory
> An interval is the distance between two notes. It has two parts: a number, found by counting letter names inclusively from the lower note to the upper, and a quality such as major, minor, perfect, augmented or diminished, which specifies the exact size in semitones.

### How to choose a double bass
https://www.accordion.sg/how-to-choose-a-double-bass.html — Buying guides
> Pick the size your hand and arm can manage, almost always 3/4 for adults. Then choose construction: plywood for durability, hybrid for a better top at moderate cost, fully carved for tone. Budget separately for a proper setup, which changes a bass more than most people expect.

### Piano accordion vs button accordion
https://www.accordion.sg/piano-accordion-vs-button-accordion.html — Accordion
> A piano accordion has a familiar keyboard and transfers easily from piano, but its keys are wide, so a full range needs a large instrument. A chromatic button accordion fits over five octaves under one hand, repeats fingerings in every key, and dominates the classical repertoire, but nothing about it is intuitive at first.

### Major and minor scales explained
https://www.accordion.sg/major-and-minor-scales-explained.html — Music theory
> A major scale is a fixed pattern of steps: tone, tone, semitone, tone, tone, tone, semitone. A minor scale lowers the third, sixth and seventh degrees of that pattern. The lowered third is what your ear hears as the difference between bright and dark.

### Dynamics and articulation, explained
https://www.accordion.sg/dynamics-and-articulation-explained.html — Music theory
> Dynamics are the markings that indicate loudness, from pianissimo through to fortissimo, together with gradual changes such as crescendo and diminuendo. Articulation describes how each note is begun and ended: detached, joined, accented or short. Dynamics shape the volume; articulation shapes the edges.

### Transposition explained
https://www.accordion.sg/transposition-explained.html — Music theory
> Transposition means moving a piece of music up or down by a fixed interval, so every note shifts by the same distance and the relationships between them stay identical. The tune sounds the same but starts on a different pitch, and the key signature usually changes to match.

### How to choose an accordion
https://www.accordion.sg/how-to-choose-an-accordion.html — Buying guides
> Choose by body size first, then repertoire. Most adults start on a 96- or 120-bass piano accordion weighing eight to eleven kilos; children need 48- or 72-bass boxes. Beyond that, pay for reed quality and a tight bellows rather than for extra buttons you will not use for years.

### How an accordion actually works
https://www.accordion.sg/how-does-an-accordion-work.html — Accordion
> An accordion makes sound with free reeds: thin steel tongues riveted over slots in metal plates. Bellows pressure sets them vibrating. Each note has two reeds, one speaking on the push and one on the pull, and register switches slide covers over reed chambers to change which ranks sound.

### What is a key signature?
https://www.accordion.sg/what-is-a-key-signature.html — Music theory
> A key signature is the group of sharps or flats printed just after the clef. It tells you which notes stay raised or lowered for the whole piece, in every octave, so the music does not need an accidental in front of every note. It also names the key you are in.
